verdicts.summary: The modelCatalogOnly early return skips the other refresh steps, and the empty providers list is never recorded or shown by callers.
verdicts.scenario: I tried five cases. (1) An old server: both call sites check capabilities.modelCatalogRefresh, and ServerEnvironment.ts:252 sets it only on new servers. (2) The empty `{providers: []}` reply overwriting client state: onSuccess returns early when instanceId or cwd is undefined, and the callers send neither. (3) The call collapsing into a full refresh or a refresh with other flags: the singleFlight key includes modelCatalogOnly. (4) Providers reading a stale cached catalog because invalidateModelCaches is skipped: ClaudeDriver reads the catalog fresh on every probe, and its Cache holds only the capabilities probe. (5) A fetch failure or `enableProviderUpdateChecks` set to false: refresh returns the current manifest, and refreshModelCatalog wraps the rest in catchCause.

verdicts.summary: The two-pass loop is bounded, and a stale or in-flight pass only costs one extra probe. No pass can be skipped wrongly.
verdicts.scenario: I tried four orderings. (1) A pass already in flight when the manifest is fetched: refreshAll joins it through the Deferred and it records the older updatedAt, so pass 2 runs and probes with the new manifest. (2) A forceRefresh from another path moves the manifest past the `updatedAt` that refreshModelCatalog captured: the equality check keeps failing, but the loop stops after 2 iterations, and the next call re-reads updatedAt. (3) A failed pass: Ref.set sits inside the tap after the probes, so the ref is not advanced and the next open retries. (4) A fetched manifest with the same updatedAt but different content: no probe runs. This relies on updatedAt being bumped on publish, which is the design intent and the same version gate ModelManifest uses at line 253.
